memoryFrontier.interpretation: Memory is classified on the same 1 GiB+ JavaScript full-string row set used for counterexample scanning; process RSS, browser JS heap, and browser host-probe-only rows are not normalized into one allocation model.

textMaterializationFrontier.interpretation: Text/CDATA omission crosses the target as headroom evidence, while trim-only, fold-trim, cache, and ASCII candidates remain negative for the current full-string contract.

sourceConsumptionFrontier.primaryLargeComparisonInput: The file-backed release comparison rows call external-baseline with --stax-stream-source file-sync-batches, which records synchronous Iterable<Uint8Array[]> parser input and directReadableStream=false.
sourceConsumptionFrontier.syncIterableInput: sync-iterable-byte-batches uses StreamReaderSync over a synchronous Iterable<Uint8Array[]> and yields one grouped batch per parser pull.
sourceConsumptionFrontier.asyncIterableInput: async-iterable-byte-batches uses StreamReader over an AsyncIterable<Uint8Array[]> and awaits one pre-grouped byte batch per parser pull.
sourceConsumptionFrontier.readableStreamInput: web-readable-stream-pull uses StreamReader over a Web ReadableStream<Uint8Array> pull source.
sourceConsumptionFrontier.readableStreamAsyncBoundary: The direct ReadableStream rows include the public StreamReader await reader.read() boundary; batchSize controls how many chunks are grouped per bounded nextBatch() operation. Throughput is source-shape evidence, not a parser/runtime ceiling for sync byte batches.
sourceConsumptionFrontier.readableStreamBackpressure: The ReadableStream source reads only inside pull(); StreamReader consumes at most the configured readable batch size per nextBatch() operation, so production remains bounded by consumer demand.
sourceConsumptionFrontier.arrayBufferConsumption: Neither measured row constructs one full XML string or one repeated 1 GiB ArrayBuffer parser input; file chunks are read on demand for the selected source shape.
sourceConsumptionFrontier.interpretation: The current large-file comparison uses demand-driven Iterable<Uint8Array[]> batches; direct ReadableStream rows are separate source-shape evidence and remain bounded by pull/read demand.

browserLiveSourceFrontier.interpretation: Browser live fetch rows consume Response.body directly or through grouped AsyncIterable<Uint8Array[]> batches under the same checksum contract; they are intentionally separate from prepared corpus-seed replay rows.

findings.summary: Rows are grouped by semantic checksum contract, while memory counters remain runtime-specific.
The same 1 GiB+ JavaScript full-string row set used for counterexample scanning is classified by memory metric and bounded-memory status.
The aggregated 1 GiB+ JavaScript full-string rows contain no 200 MiB/s bounded-memory counterexample.
The fastest bounded 1 GiB+ public event-object row is tracked separately from raw-frame rows.
Recognized 1 GiB+ JavaScript full-string source-mode rows are classified for full XML ArrayBuffer parser input.
The external baselines keep Woodstox and quick-xml visible as non-JS comparators under the same checksum contract.
The nearest full-string row, text/CDATA omission headroom, and negative text-materialization candidates remain visible in the aggregate comparison.
The aggregate comparison links the sync byte-batch baseline, async byte-batch rows, direct ReadableStream rows, and backpressure counters.
Chrome live fetch ReadableStream and grouped async byte-batch rows remain visible separately from prepared corpus-seed replay rows.
